The issue says hovering another taskbar icon preview should make the pinned window outline disappear, but the outline remains visible.
A commenter says the real reason is the same family as a desktop/show-desktop behavior and points to a newer issue.
inferences: The taskbar preview and Win+D scenarios likely share the same missing hidden-window border lifecycle handling.
The newer Win+D report is a better anchor for design and testing because it is deterministic and does not depend on shell preview timing.

comment.body: Thanks for the screenshot and taskbar-preview repro. This appears to be the same hidden-window border persistence family as #49785, which reproduces it more directly with Win+D: the pinned window is effectively hidden, but the Always On Top border remains visible and detached. Please consolidate this report with #49785 so the border-lifecycle investigation stays in one place.
